subject.title: Bounded memory tool with hard character limits

question: Should OpenClaw define a first-class bounded memory write/CRUD contract in memory-core, and what hard-limit, identity, duplicate/consolidation, snapshot, config, and secret-handling semantics should it expose?
rationale: Current source proves the capability is still missing, but adding it creates public memory-write, config, persistence, prompt-context, and security behavior that automation cannot safely choose.

options.title: Define bounded memory-core CRUD
options.body: Approve an add/list/replace/remove or unified memory tool with hard per-store limits, usage feedback, stable identity, duplicate/consolidation behavior, secret policy, docs, and focused regression coverage.

options.title: Limit scope to existing safety nets
options.body: Continue with bounded dreaming promotion, memory-flush append validation, and visibility/warning work while leaving general CRUD writes out of the default memory tool surface for now.

options.title: Prototype outside the default contract
options.body: Prove the write API and safety policy in a memory plugin or operator-facing prototype before promoting it into the default memory-core contract.

recommendation.title: Define bounded memory-core CRUD
recommendation.body: Approve an add/list/replace/remove or unified memory tool with hard per-store limits, usage feedback, stable identity, duplicate/consolidation behavior, secret policy, docs, and focused regression coverage.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision spans product direction, public API shape, configuration, persistence, and security boundaries across the memory system.
